(Glenview, Illinois) | college = [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] (2022–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 55 | draft_team = [[New York Knicks]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | highlights = * 2× Second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2025]], [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2026]]) * 2× First-team [[Academic All-American]] ([[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025]], [[2026 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2026]]) | team2 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | years2 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present }} '''Nicholas Joseph Martinelli''' (born April 20, 2004){{Cite web |title=ESPN Player Biography - Nick Martinelli |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/bio/_/id/5105832/nick-martinelli |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=www.espn.com}} is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern Wildcats]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. Martinelli was a two-time second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honoree by the Big Ten Conference coaches and media, 2-time first-team [[Academic All-America]] selection, and a two-time Big Ten scoring champion. He also earned [[Associated Press]] 1st-team All-Big Ten recognition in 2026. He was also a member of the only Northwestern teams to earn back-to-back [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] invitations. He set the Northwestern single-season scoring record. At [[Glenbrook South High School]], he was a two-time Associated Press All-State honoree (2021 2nd-team, 2022 1st-team). == High school career == Martinelli's parents are named Jim and Carolyn. The Martinellis had a basketball [[Basket (basketball)|hoop]] in their driveway.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2019/03/06/dom-martinelli-will-king-anchor-glenbrook-souths-special-season/|title=Dom Martinelli, Will King anchor Glenbrook South’s special season|accessdate=May 1, 2026|date=March 19, 2026|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Sadin, Steve}} Nick started attending Northwestern basketball camps in fifth or sixth grade and played against his older brothers.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/3313378929|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|3313378929}}|title=As Martinelli's Northwestern career ends, brother recalls how|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=1|author=|accessdate=May 2, 2026|date=March 13, 2026}} Martinelli attended [[Glenbrook South High School]] in [[Glenview, Illinois]]. He is the younger brother of All-state player and [[Illinois High School Association]] record book achiever [[Dominic Martinelli]].{{cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/1/30/21116079/glenbrook-south-evanston-high-school-basketball-dominic-martinelli|title=Martinelli brothers, Cooper Noard lead Glenbrook South to statement win against Evanston|accessdate=April 29, 2026|date=January 30, 2020|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=O'Brien, Michael}}{{cite web|url=https://www.ihsa.org/data/bkb/records/aindiv.htm|title=IHSA Boys Basketball All-Time Individual Records|accessdate=April 29, 2026|date=April 26, 2026|publisher=[[Illinois High School Association]]}} Oldest brother Jimmy, who was a Glenbrook South team [[captain (sports)|captain]], was a good player on sub-.500 teams at the school. He started for [[NYU Violets men's basketball|NYU]] from 2016 through 2020.{{cite web|url=https://gonyuathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jimmy-martinelli/12249|title=33: Jimmy Martinelli|accessdate=April 30, 2026|publisher=[[NYU Violets]]}} Nick preferred [[American football]] and [[baseball]] to basketball when he was younger. He was mentioned in the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' in 2017 as a member of the 41-8-1 13U Glenview Blaze team which won the Midwest Suburban Baseball League's (MSBL) and was the regular season champion of the MSBL's top conference.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1923719392|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1923719392}}|title=Champions - 13U Glenview Blaze|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|page=|author=|accessdate=May 2, 2026|date=July 25, 2017}} Martinelli had endured years of Glenbrook South mediocrity while cheering on his older brothers Jimmy who graduated in 2016 and Dom who was in the class of 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2021/12/17/elon-recruit-nick-martinelli-isnt-juggling-priorities-this-season-its-all-about-winning-for-glenbrook-souths-6-foot-8-forward/|title=Elon recruit Nick Martinelli isn’t juggling priorities this season. ‘It’s all about winning’ for Glenbrook South’s 6-foot-8 forward.|accessdate=May 1, 2026|date=December 17, 2021|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Millar, Steve}} He even joined the varsity team as a sophomore and played with Dom. Thus, Nick had an 86-game varsity career.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2637590520|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2637590520}}|title=Remember these Titans|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=22|author=Oberhelman, Dave|accessdate=May 3, 2026|date=March 10, 2022}} Prior to the 2018-19 season (Nick's freshman year) Glenbrook South had had only 1 10-win season in the prior 4 and one 15-win season since 2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2018/12/02/glenbrook-south-breaks-through-with-signature-win-against-evanston/|title=Glenbrook South breaks through with signature win against Evanston|accessdate=May 1, 2026|date=December 2, 2018|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Narang, Bob}} That year, Dom helped Glenbrook South turn around a 9-19 record from the previous season (and back-to-back 9-win seasons) into a 24-win season and an IHSA Class 4A regional championship.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2019/03/03/boys-basketball-notes-dom-martinelli-pilots-glenbrook-south-past-niles-west/|title=Boys basketball notes: Dom Martinelli pilots Glenbrook South past Niles West|accessdate=May 1, 2026|date=March 3, 2019|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Narang, Bob}} Nick played [[center (basketball)|center]] in high school. One of his earliest moments in the basketball spotlight came as a sophomore in a February 21, 2020, overtime game against [[Evanston Township High School]], when he was fouled on a game-tying [[three point shot]] [[buzzer beater]] attempt. After making the first two and enduring a [[time-out (sport)|time-out]], he missed the final free throw. This opened the door for Evanston to have a share of the Central Suburban League South division. The teams split the season series, and both teams finished with 9–1 division records.{{cite web|url=https://evanstonroundtable.com/2020/02/22/boys-b-ball-team-beats-titans-in-overtime/|title=Boys B-ball Team Beats Titans in Overtime|accessdate=May 1, 2026|date=February 22, 2020|work=Evanston Roundtable|author=Mahoney, Dennis}} Glenbrook South moved to a 29–4 record with a 65–49 win against [[Maine West High School]] in the Class 4A Regional championship on March 6, 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/03/08/glenbrook-souths-dom-martinelli-looking-for-best-college-fit/|title=Glenbrook South’s Dom Martinelli looking for best college fit|accessdate=May 1, 2026|date=March 8, 2020|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Narang, Bob}} Glenbrook South lost to Evanston 62–57 in the Class 4A sectional against Evanston to finish 29–5.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2375864971|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2375864971}}|title=Cook County scoreboard Tuesday, March 10|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=|author=|accessdate=May 2, 2026|date=March 11, 2020}} His 2020–21 junior season was truncated by a second wave of COVID-19 that delayed the IHSA Winter Sports from November to February.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2486152255|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2486152255}}|title=Biggest point of the game? They’re playing|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=|author=Oberhelman, Dave|accessdate=May 2, 2026|date=February 4, 2021}} Glenbrook South opened its season on February 3. As a junior, he averaged 21.8 points and 5.9 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |last=Moreano |first=Nicholas |date=March 24, 2021 |title=Nick Martinelli's inner fighter has shaped who he has become as a basketball player |url=https://illinois-basketball.com/nick-martinelli-glenbrook-south-fighter/ |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Illinois High School Basketball |language=en-US}}{{Cite web web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2627170530|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2627170530}}|title=Titans claim ‘uncharted territory’ with win over Curie|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington school's 60-year history with a 55–52 victory over New Trier on Glenbrook South's home court.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2636750997|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2636750997}}|title=Glenbrook S. nips New Trier for sectional crown|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, 1,450 by Brad Niemann){{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/05/02/recruiting-notes-glenbrook-south-forward-dom-martinelli-to-walk-on-at-northwestern/|title=Recruiting notes: Glenbrook He was named to the 2022 [[Associated Press]] Class 4A First-Team All-State along with [[Braden Huff]], [[Owen Freeman]], [[Dai Dai Ames]] and AJ Casey.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/entertainment-sports-basketball-illinois-high-school-basketball-aabe1472e149d2c0f504965b64869c70|title=Illinois Boys All-State Basketball Teams|accessdate=December and Ty Rodgers.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2655611777|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2655611777}}|title=2022 Mr. and Ms. Basketball of Illinois winners: Braden Huff of Illinois for 2020|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|page=|author=Prince, DeAntae|accessdate=May 2, 2026|date=April 17, 2020}} Martinelli originally committed to [[Elon University]] to play under head coach [[Mike Schrage]].{{Cite web |last=Oberhelman |first=Dave |date=July 14, 2021 |title=Glenbrook South's Nick Martinelli makes early college basketball decision |url=https://www.dailyherald.com/20210714/boys-basketball/glenbrook-souths-nick-martinelli-makes-early-college-basketball-decision/ |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Daily Herald |language=en-US}} After Schrage resigned as head coach at Elon, Martinelli decommitted from the Phoenix,{{Cite web |date=April 12, 2022 |title=Nick Martinelli’s recruitment soars after emotional parting with Elon |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2022/4/12/23021794/nick-martinelli-glenbrook-south-elon-basketball |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Chicago Sun-Times |language=en}} citing both Shrage's April 5 resignation and [[Andrew Dakich]]'s March 30 departure.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2650004022|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2650004022}}|title=Nick Martinelli back on the market|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=21|author=Oberhelman, Dave|accessdate=May 3, 2026|date=April 14, 2022}} After decommitting he picked up at least ten scholarship offers and held serious conversations with [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]]. Due to the familiarity of Northwestern basketball whose players he often participated in [[pick-up game]]s with and whose coaches had seen dozens of his games as a deciding factor,{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2656216034|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2656216034}}|title=‘This is where I want to go; this is where I want to be’|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=|author=Oberhelman, Dave|accessdate=May 3, 2026|date=April 28, 2022}} the three-star recruit committed to play college basketball at [[Northwestern University]].{{Cite web |title=Collins Announces Addition of Martinelli |url=https://nusports.com/news/2022/4/28/mens-basketball-collins-announces-addition-of-martinelli |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Northwestern Athletics |language=en}} Northwestern head basketball coach [[Chris Collins (basketball)|Chris Collins]] had been 1992 Illinois Mr. Basketball at nearby rival [[Glenbrook North High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2627170530|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2627170530}}|title=Nick Martinelli’s ‘unorthodox’ game and confidence is a bright spot in an up-and-down Northwestern season|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|page=|author=Kane, Colleen|accessdate=May 3, 2026|date=February 24, 2025}} Assistant coach [[Brian James (basketball)|Brian James]] was also a Glenbrook North alumnus. == College career == [[File:20260211 Elliot Cadeau defending Nick Martinelli.jpg|thumb|Martinelli attacking [[Elliot Cadeau]] in 2026]] Martinelli played sparingly as a freshman,{{Cite web |last=Epstein |first=Jake |date=November 11, 2023 |title=Northwestern’s Nick Martinelli looks to make second-year leap |url=https://dailynorthwestern.com/2023/11/11/lateststories/mens-basketball-looking-to-make-second-year-leap-martinelli-helps-push-northwestern-past-dayton/ |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=The Daily Northwestern}} but he led all freshmen in scoring (2.6 points per game) and minutes. His 9 points on 3–3 three point shooting against [[2022–23 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] on January 31, 2023, was his season high. He appeared in 20 games, including the final 17.{{cite web|url=https://nusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/nick-martinelli/12688|title=2: Nick Martinelli|accessdate=May 3, 2026|publisher=[[Northwestern Wildcats]]}} Julian Roper II injured his ankle and missed most of the 2nd half of the season, as Martinelli earned minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/julian-roper-player|title=Julian Roper News|accessdate=May 3, 2026|date=|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]}} The [[2016–17 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|2016–17 Wildcats]] had been the first Northwestern team to make the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. Then, Northwestern endured 5 consecutive losing seasons before the [[2022–23 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|2022–23 team]] was invited to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2787217665|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2787217665}}|title=Can Cats capitalize on program’s 2nd tourney berth?|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|page=22|author=Gregor, Scot|accessdate=May 4, 2026|date=March 16, 2023}} Martinelli's role increased as a sophomore.{{Cite web |last=McGraw |first=Mike |date=March 13, 2024 |title=Little brother life pushed Martinelli to become NU’s super sub |url=https://www.dailyherald.com/20240313/college-sports/little-brother-life-pushed-martinelli-to-become-nus-super-sub/ |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Daily Herald |language=en-US}} On web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401581721|title=Martinelli's career-high 22 leads Northwestern past Detroit Mercy 91-59|accessdate=May 4, 2026|date=December 10,
